summary: Iteration 4 testing complete. GitHub Releases tracker is fully functional end-to-end. All 35 backend pytest cases pass (7 new TestReleases tests added) and frontend ReleaseTracker integration verified on /tool/palera1n (verified mode) and /tool/checkra1n (unavailable fallback).
critical_code_review_comments: releases_router.py: when GitHub returns 404 on /releases/latest, fallback to /tags is good but discards subsequent error handling; if tags also returns non-200/empty list, the code calls resp.raise_for_status() on the original 404 response which is fine. Minor: HTTPException 502 detail leaks the upstream status code which is OK for a public dev API but could be tightened.

releases_router.py: stale-cache fallback on HTTPStatusError is great, but a stale entry served from the catch-block bypasses TTL silently with no indication to the client. Consider adding a `stale: true` flag on the response so the UI can show a 'cached' badge.
releases_router.py: GITHUB_TOKEN is read fresh on every request via os.environ.get; inexpensive but worth caching at module load if env isn't expected to change.

ReleaseTracker.jsx: `info.html_url` may be null for the tag-only fallback path when has_tracker=true but no release exists; the github-link href would render as 'null'. Low priority — only triggers when GITHUB_REPOS contains a repo with no releases AND no tags, which currently doesn't happen.

ReleaseTracker.jsx: error state covers the catch path but does not distinguish a 502 (upstream rate limit) from an actual network failure. A friendlier message like 'GitHub rate-limited — try again in a minute' would help during heavy testing.
release_cache collection: no TTL index on `fetched_at`. Stale records linger forever for tools removed from GITHUB_REPOS. Cosmetic; not user-visible.
test_credentials: N/A - no auth in this app.
seed_data_creation: Real GitHub API calls cached MongoDB documents in 'release_cache' collection for tool_ids: palera1n, dopamine, roothide, checkra1n, unc0ver, xinaA15. No cleanup needed (10-min TTL, idempotent upsert).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Iteration 4 added TestReleases (7 cases) to /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py: palera1n/dopamine/roothide return has_tracker=true with valid repo + tag + assets[] containing GitHub /releases/download/ URLs; parametrised test for checkra1n/unc0ver/xinaA15 returns has_tracker=false, repo=None; cache test asserts second call within TTL returns identical fetched_at and ?refresh=true returns a strictly newer fetched_at. All asset.download_url values verified to start with https://github.com/.../releases/download/. Frontend data-testids: release-tracker, release-tracker-loading, release-tracker-unavailable, release-tracker-error, release-tag, release-github-link, release-refresh, release-asset-{i}, release-asset-download-{i}, release-notes. ReleaseTracker is rendered inside ToolDetail under the section kicker '00 · Release.tracker' with heading 'Latest verified release'. Tests tolerate occasional 502 from GitHub rate limiting via pytest.skip — re-run if hit.
rca of the issue: No issues found. Live verification: palera1n returned tag v2.2.1 with 9 binary assets including palera1n-linux-arm64 (and x86_64, macOS). Refresh button produced 'Release info refreshed' toast and the new fetched_at was strictly greater than cached value. checkra1n correctly showed the 'No live release tracker for this tool' fallback box. Release notes <details> expands on click. No regression on existing endpoints (TestRoot, TestTools, TestCompatibility, TestChat etc. all green).
